name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q01 - Sequence of molar conductivity in cobalt ammine complexes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following coordination compounds investigated by Alfred Werner:

  1. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 6NH_3}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 5NH_3}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 4NH_3}\)
  4. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 3NH_3}\)

Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of electrical conductivity of their equimolar aqueous solutions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Werner's formulations and electrolyte types
According to Werner's theory, only ions located outside the coordination sphere dissociate into free mobile ions in aqueous solution, which determine electrical conductivity.

Step 2: Number of ions produced in solution
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 6NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}\) and dissociates into 4 ions (\(1:3\) electrolyte: \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) and \(3\mathrm{Cl^-}\)).
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 5NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2}\) and dissociates into 3 ions (\(1:2\) electrolyte: \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]^{2+}}\) and \(2\mathrm{Cl^-}\)).
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 4NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]Cl}\) and dissociates into 2 ions (\(1:1\) electrolyte: \(\mathrm{[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]^+}\) and \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\)).
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 3NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl_3(NH_3)_3]}\) and is a non-electrolyte yielding 0 free ions.

Step 3: Determination of the sequence
Because electrical conductivity in equimolar solutions increases with the total number of ions produced per formula unit, the decreasing order of electrical conductivity is: \[ \mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3} > \mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2} > \mathrm{[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]Cl} > \mathrm{[CoCl_3(NH_3)_3]} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence corresponds to \(\mathrm{I > II > III > IV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q02 - Sequence of ligands in spectrochemical series

questiontext.text:
The spectrochemical series arranges ligands in order of increasing crystal field splitting energy (\(\Delta_\mathrm{o}\)). Consider the following four ligands:

  1. \(\mathrm{Br^-}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{F^-}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)
  4. \(\mathrm{CN^-}\)

Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their ligand field strength?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Spectrochemical series definition
The spectrochemical series is an experimentally determined sequence based on the absorption spectra of coordination complexes with different ligands, arranging ligands in order of increasing \(\Delta_\mathrm{o}\).

Step 2: Canonical order in the textbook
The NCERT spectrochemical series is: \[ \mathrm{I^- < Br^- < SCN^- < Cl^- < S^{2-} < F^- < OH^- < C_2O_4^{2-} < H_2O < NCS^- < edta^{4-} < NH_3 < en < CN^- < CO} \]

Step 3: Ordering the selected ligands
Extracting the given four ligands: \[ \mathrm{Br^- < F^- < H_2O < CN^-} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The sequence from weakest to strongest ligand field strength is \(\mathrm{I < II < III < IV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q03 - Chronological sequence of colour changes in nickel ethylenediamine system

questiontext.text:
When the didentate ligand ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{en}\)) is progressively added to an aqueous solution containing \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\) in molar ratios of \(\mathrm{en : Ni}\) equal to \(1:1\), \(2:1\), and \(3:1\), distinct sequential colour changes occur:

  1. Formation of \(\mathrm{[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}(aq)}\)
  2. Formation of \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+}(aq)}\)
  3. Initial hydrated cation \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}(aq)}\)
  4. Formation of \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+}(aq)}\)

What is the correct sequential order of the appearance of these species as \(\mathrm{en}\) is progressively added, and what is the corresponding sequence of observed colours?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical reactions of sequential ligand substitution
When ethane-1,2-diamine is added successively to an aqueous nickel(II) solution: 1. Initially, the hexaaqua ion exists alone: \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\), which is green. 2. At a molar ratio of \(\mathrm{en : Ni} = 1:1\), two aqua ligands are displaced: \[ \mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+} + en \rightarrow [Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+} + 2H_2O} \quad (\text{pale blue}) \] 3. At a molar ratio of \(\mathrm{en : Ni} = 2:1\), another two aqua ligands are displaced: \[ \mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+} + en \rightarrow [Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+} + 2H_2O} \quad (\text{blue / purple}) \] 4. At a molar ratio of \(\mathrm{en : Ni} = 3:1\), all remaining aqua ligands are displaced: \[ \mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+} + en \rightarrow [Ni(en)_3]^{2+} + 2H_2O} \quad (\text{violet}) \]

Step 2: Species sequence
The sequential chronological appearance of species is \(\mathrm{III \rightarrow II \rightarrow IV \rightarrow I}\).

Step 3: Colour sequence
The corresponding observed colour progression is Green \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Violet.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence of species is \(\mathrm{III \rightarrow II \rightarrow IV \rightarrow I}\) with the progression Green \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Violet.

answer.text: \(\mathrm{III \rightarrow II \rightarrow IV \rightarrow I}\) (Green \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Violet)
\(\mathrm{III \rightarrow IV \rightarrow II \rightarrow I}\) (Green \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Violet)
\(\mathrm{II \rightarrow III \rightarrow IV \rightarrow I}\) (Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Green \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Violet)
\(\mathrm{III \rightarrow II \rightarrow I \rightarrow IV}\) (Green \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Violet \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q04 - Sequence of absorption wavelength in nickel complexes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following octahedral complexes of nickel(II):

  1. \(\mathrm{[Ni(NO_2)_6]^{4-}}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\)

Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of wavelength of light absorbed (\(\lambda_\mathrm{max}\)) in the visible region by these complexes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relationship between crystal field splitting and absorption wavelength
The energy of light absorbed during a \(d\text{-}d\) transition is given by \(\Delta_\mathrm{o} = \frac{hc}{\lambda}\). Therefore, the wavelength of absorption is inversely proportional to the crystal field splitting energy: \[ \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\Delta_\mathrm{o}} \]

Step 2: Relative ligand field strength
According to the spectrochemical series, the order of field strength of the ligands is: \[ \mathrm{H_2O < NH_3 < NO_2^-} \]

Step 3: Order of crystal field splitting energy (\(\Delta_\mathrm{o}\))
Because the central metal ion is \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) in all three complexes, the splitting magnitude depends strictly on the ligand field strength: \[ \Delta_\mathrm{o}(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}) < \Delta_\mathrm{o}(\mathrm{[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}) < \Delta_\mathrm{o}(\mathrm{[Ni(NO_2)_6]^{4-}}) \]

Step 4: Decreasing order of absorption wavelength
Inverting the \(\Delta_\mathrm{o}\) values yields the order of wavelengths of absorbed light: \[ \lambda(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}) > \lambda(\mathrm{[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}) > \lambda(\mathrm{[Ni(NO_2)_6]^{4-}}) \]

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The decreasing order of absorption wavelength is \(\mathrm{III > II > I}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q05 - Logical sequence of steps in gold extraction via cyanide complexation

questiontext.text:
The extraction of metallic gold from its native ore involves the following chemical operations:

  1. Oxidative leaching of finely crushed gold ore with an aqueous \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) solution in the presence of air and water
  2. Filtration to separate the soluble coordination complex \(\mathrm{[Au(CN)_2]^-}\) from insoluble gangue
  3. Displacement reaction by addition of powdered zinc to reduce gold(I) to elemental gold
  4. Separation and purification of the precipitated metallic gold from the solution containing \(\mathrm{[Zn(CN)_4]^{2-}}\)

What is the correct logical sequence of these steps in the industrial metallurgical process?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Industrial metallurgy of gold via coordination entities
The MacArthur-Forrest cyanide process relies on complexation and subsequent displacement of gold.

Step 2: Step-by-step reaction progression
1. Finely crushed ore is leached with dilute cyanide solution in the presence of atmospheric oxygen, oxidising insoluble gold to the soluble aurocyanide complex: \[ 4\mathrm{Au} + 8\mathrm{CN^-} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{[Au(CN)_2]^-} + 4\mathrm{OH^-} \] 2. The mixture is filtered to obtain a clear pregnant solution containing the coordination entity \(\mathrm{[Au(CN)_2]^-}\), separating it from undissolved rock/gangue.
3. Zinc dust is added to the filtered solution. Being more electropositive, zinc acts as a reducing agent and displaces gold: \[ 2\mathrm{[Au(CN)_2]^-} + \mathrm{Zn} \rightarrow \mathrm{[Zn(CN)_4]^{2-}} + 2\mathrm{Au}\downarrow \] 4. The precipitated elemental gold is filtered, washed, and refined.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct operational sequence is \(\mathrm{I \rightarrow II \rightarrow III \rightarrow IV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q06 - Sequence of spin only magnetic moments in high spin complexes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following high-spin coordination complexes in aqueous solution:

  1. \(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\)
  4. \(\mathrm{[Zn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\)

Which of the following represents the correct decreasing sequence of their spin-only magnetic moments (\(\mu_\mathrm{s}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula for spin-only magnetic moment
The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated as \(\mu_\mathrm{s} = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\,\mathrm{BM}\), where \(n\) is the number of unpaired electrons in the complex entity.

Step 2: Electronic configuration and number of unpaired electrons
1. In \(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\), iron is \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) (\(3d^5\)). Because \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) is a weak field ligand, electrons occupy \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^2\), giving \(n = 5\) unpaired electrons: \[ \mu_\mathrm{s} = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\,\mathrm{BM} \] 2. In \(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\), iron is \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) (\(3d^6\)). In a weak field, the configuration is \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^2\), giving \(n = 4\) unpaired electrons: \[ \mu_\mathrm{s} = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\,\mathrm{BM} \] 3. In \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\), chromium is \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) (\(3d^3\)). The configuration is \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^0\), giving \(n = 3\) unpaired electrons: \[ \mu_\mathrm{s} = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87\,\mathrm{BM} \] 4. In \(\mathrm{[Zn(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\), zinc is \(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}\) (\(3d^{10}\)). All five \(d\) orbitals are completely filled (\(t_{2g}^6 e_g^4\)), giving \(n = 0\) unpaired electrons: \[ \mu_\mathrm{s} = 0\,\mathrm{BM} \]

Step 3: Ordering by magnetic moment
Comparing the calculated values: \[ 5.92\,\mathrm{BM} \;(\mathrm{I}) > 4.90\,\mathrm{BM} \;(\mathrm{II}) > 3.87\,\mathrm{BM} \;(\mathrm{III}) > 0\,\mathrm{BM} \;(\mathrm{IV}) \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The decreasing sequence is \(\mathrm{I > II > III > IV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q07 - Sequence of crystal field stabilization energies for octahedral d configurations

questiontext.text:
Consider the following octahedral complex ions containing strong field ligands (\(\Delta_\mathrm{o} > P\)):

  1. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) (\(d^6\) low-spin)
  2. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}\) (\(d^5\) low-spin)
  3. \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}\) (\(d^4\) low-spin)
  4. \(\mathrm{[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}}\) (\(d^3\))

Which of the following represents the correct decreasing sequence of the magnitude of their crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE, ignoring pairing energy)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula for crystal field stabilization energy in octahedral fields
For an octahedral complex with configuration \(t_{2g}^x e_g^y\), the crystal field stabilization energy is: \[ \mathrm{CFSE} = \left( -0.4\,x + 0.6\,y \right)\Delta_\mathrm{o} \]

Step 2: Evaluation for each configuration
1. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\): Central ion is \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) (\(d^6\)). With strong field \(\mathrm{NH_3}\), all electrons pair in the lower set to give \(t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\): \[ |\mathrm{CFSE}| = |-0.4 \times 6|\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} = 2.4\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \] 2. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}\): Central ion is \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) (\(d^5\)). With strong field \(\mathrm{CN^-}\), the configuration is \(t_{2g}^5 e_g^0\): \[ |\mathrm{CFSE}| = |-0.4 \times 5|\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} = 2.0\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \] 3. \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}\): Central ion is \(\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}\) (\(d^4\)). With strong field \(\mathrm{CN^-}\), the configuration is \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^0\): \[ |\mathrm{CFSE}| = |-0.4 \times 4|\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} = 1.6\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \] 4. \(\mathrm{[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}}\): Central ion is \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) (\(d^3\)). The configuration is \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^0\): \[ |\mathrm{CFSE}| = |-0.4 \times 3|\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} = 1.2\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \]

Step 3: Ordering the magnitudes
Comparing the CFSE magnitudes: \[ 2.4\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \;(\mathrm{I}) > 2.0\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \;(\mathrm{II}) > 1.6\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \;(\mathrm{III}) > 1.2\,\Delta_\mathrm{o} \;(\mathrm{IV}) \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The decreasing sequence of CFSE magnitude is \(\mathrm{I > II > III > IV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q08 - Sequence of carbon oxygen bond strength in synergically bonded metal carbonyls

questiontext.text:
The extent of \(\mathrm{M \rightarrow CO}\) \(\pi\)-back donation in isoelectronic hexacarbonyl species directly influences the \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond strength and bond order. Consider the following isoelectronic series:

  1. \(\mathrm{[Mn(CO)_6]^+}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{[V(CO)_6]^-}\)

Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond strength (stretching frequency) in these carbonyl complexes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of synergic bonding and C-O bond order
In metal carbonyls, \(\pi\)-back donation involves transfer of electron density from filled metal \(d\) orbitals into the vacant antibonding \(\pi^*\) molecular orbitals of carbon monoxide. As electron density in the \(\pi^*\) antibonding orbital increases, the \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond order, bond strength, and stretching frequency decrease, while the \(\mathrm{M-C}\) bond strength increases.

Step 2: Effect of formal charge on the metal centre
All three complexes are octahedral, homoleptic hexacarbonyls with the central metal possessing a \(d^6\) configuration: 1. In \(\mathrm{[V(CO)_6]^-}\), the metal carries a negative charge (\(-1\)), which raises the energy of the metal \(d\) orbitals and maximizes electron back-donation into the \(\pi^*\) orbitals of \(\mathrm{CO}\). This results in the greatest weakening of the \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond (lowest \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond strength). 2. In neutral \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]}\), back-donation occurs to a moderate extent. 3. In \(\mathrm{[Mn(CO)_6]^+}\), the positive charge (\(+1\)) on the manganese centre contracts the \(d\) orbitals and binds the metal electrons tightly, minimizing \(\pi\)-back donation into \(\mathrm{CO}\). Consequently, the antibonding population in \(\mathrm{CO}\) remains lowest, yielding the highest \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond order, highest bond strength, and highest stretching frequency.

Step 3: Ordering C-O bond strength
The strength of the \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond decreases as: \[ \mathrm{[Mn(CO)_6]^+} > \mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]} > \mathrm{[V(CO)_6]^-} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct decreasing sequence of \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond strength is \(\mathrm{I > II > III}\).
